Lemma 3.12: Core for $\bm{A}_\mathtt{PDO}[\bm\psi], \bm{\psi}\in\mathbf{N}^d_+(\mathbb R)$
nodes.statement:
\phantomsection
	Let the closure of $(B,\mathcal D)$ be the generator of a $\mathcal{C}_0$-contraction semigroup on a Banach space ${\rm X}$. Let  $(A,\mathbf{D}(A))$ be a  densely defined operator on ${\rm X}$ such that
	\begin{align}\phantomsection
		A\Lambda =\Lambda B  \ \mbox{ on } \ \mathcal D
	\end{align}
	where $\Lambda \in \mathscr{B}({\rm X})$ with dense range, and $A$ is dissipative on $\Lambda(\mathcal D)$. Then, the closure of $(A,\Lambda(\mathcal D))$ generates a $\mathcal{C}_0$-contraction semigroup on ${\rm X}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.2: $\forall{\bm\psi}\in\mathbf{N}^d_b(\mathbb R), \forall M\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb R)$…
nodes.statement:
\phantomsection
		\begin{enumerate}
\item \phantomsection
The closure of  $(\bm{A}_\mathtt{PDO}[\bm\psi_0],\mathbf{C}^\infty_c(\mathbb R^d))$ in $\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb R^d,{\bf e})$, denoted by $\bm{A}_2[\bm\psi_0]$, generates a self-adjoint $\mathcal{C}_0$-semigroup $\bm{Q} \in \mathcal{C}^+_0(\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,{\mathbf{e}}))$.
More specifically, $\bm{Q}$ restricted to  $\mathbf{C}_0(\mathbb R^d)\cap \mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb R^d,{\bf e})$  extends to the Feller semigroup of the $d$-dimensional log-Bessel process of dimension 2 whose generator is the closure of $(\bm{A}_0, \mathbf{C}^\infty_c(\mathbb R^d))$.
	\item \phantomsection
For any $M\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb R)$, there exists a one-to-one mapping between the set $\mathscr{A}_M$ and the set
\[ \mathscr{P}_M=\left\{\bm{P}^M[\bm{\psi}]; \: \bm{\psi}\in\mathbf{N}^d_b(\mathbb{R})\right\} \subset \mathcal{C}_0(\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,{\mathbf{e}}_M))\]
such that $\bm{A}^M_\mathtt{2}[\bm\psi]=\bm{A}^M_\mathtt{PDO}[\bm\psi]$ on a dense subset, where  $\bm{A}^M_\mathtt{2}[\bm\psi]$ is the  $\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb R^d,\mathbf{e}_M)$-generator of $\bm{P}^M[\bm{\psi}]$.

More specifically,  for any ${\psi}\in \mathbf{N}_+(\mathbb R)$, $A_\mathtt{2}[\psi]$ is the closure of $(A_\mathtt{PDO}[\psi],\Lambda_{\psi}(\mathbf{C}^\infty_c(\mathbb R))$, where $\Lambda_{\psi}\in  \mathscr{B}(\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R},{e}))$ is defined in (2.3), and, otherwise, for any ${\psi}\in \mathbf{N}_b(\mathbb R)\setminus \mathbf{N}_+(\mathbb R)$, $\widehat{{P}}[{\psi}]={P}[{\overline{{\psi}}}]$. The general case is then obtained by tensorization and isomorphism of Hilbert spaces.
	\item \phantomsection 
For any $M\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb R)$, we have
\hypertarget{C16}{
	\begin{equation} \phantomsection
		\mathrm{WS}_{\mathscr{P}_M}(\bm{Q})=\mathscr{P}_M.      
	\end{equation}}
In fact, the set of weak similarity operators is a multiplicative group which entails that $\mathrm{WS}_{\mathscr{P}}$ forms an equivalence class, where $\mathscr{P}=\bigcup_{M\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb R)}\mathscr{P}_M$. 




			\item \phantomsection For any $\bm\psi\in\mathbf{N}^d_b(\mathbb R)$, we have $\widehat{\bm{P}}^M[\bm{\psi}]=\bm{P}^{M}[\overline{\bm{\psi}}]\in \mathscr{P}$, where $\widehat{\bm{P}}^M[\bm{\psi}]$ stands for  the $\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,{\mathbf{e}}_M)$-adjoint of $\bm{P}^M[\bm{\psi}]$. Thus, $\bm{P}^M[\bm{\psi}]$ is self-adjoint in $\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,{\mathbf{e}}_M)$ if and only if $\overline{\bm{\psi}}=\bm{\psi}$. \vspace{.2cm}
		\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Theorem 2.4: Spectral representation
nodes.statement:
\phantomsection
	Let $\bm{P}^M[\bm{\psi}] \in \mathscr{P}_M$ for some $M\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb R)$ and $\bm{\psi}=(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_d)\in\mathbf{N}^d_b(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\psi_k(\xi)=\phi_{+,k}(-\mathrm{i}\xi)\phi_{-,k}(\mathrm{i}\xi)$ for all $1\leqslant k\leqslant d$ and $\xi\in\mathbb{R}$. Then, for all $t\geqslant 0$, 
		\begin{align}\phantomsection
			\bm{P}^M_t[\bm{\psi}] =\bm{H}_{\bm{\psi},M}\bm{e}_t \bm{H}^{-1}_{\bm{\psi},M} \ \mbox{ on } \ \mathbf{D}(\bm{H}^{-1}_{\bm{\psi},M})
		\end{align}
		where  $\mathbf{D}(\bm{H}^{-1}_{\bm{\psi},M})=\operatorname{Range}(\bm{H}_{\bm{\psi},M})$ is dense in $\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbf{e}), \
		\bm{H}_{\bm{\psi},M}\mathbf{f}(\bm x)=\bm{H_\psi}\mathbf{f}(M \bm x)$ and $\bm{H}_{\bm{\psi}}$ being the shifted Fourier  operator with  multiplier denoted by $\mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{e}}_{\bm \psi}(\bm \xi)$, where
		\begin{equation}\phantomsection
			\mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{e}}_{\bm \psi}(\bm \xi)=\prod_{k=1}^d\frac{W_{\phi_{+,k}}(\frac{1}{2}-{\rm{i}}\xi_k)}{W_{\phi_{-,k}}(\frac{1}{2}+{\rm i}\xi_k)},\ \ \bm{\xi}=(\xi_1, \ldots,\xi_d)\in\mathbb{R}^d.
		\end{equation}
		In fact,
		\[\mathbf{D}(\bm{H}^{-1}_{\bm{\psi},M})=\left\{\mathbf{f}\in\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,{\mathbf{e}}_M);\ \bm{\xi}=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_d) \mapsto\mathcal{F}^{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathbf{f}\circ M^{-1}}(\bm{\xi})\prod_{k=1}^d\frac{W_{\phi_{-,k}}(\frac{1}{2}-{\rm{i}}\xi  _k)}{W_{\phi_{+,k}}(\frac{1}{2}+{\rm{i}}\xi  _k)}\in\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d)\right\}. \]
		Under some conditions (see Proposition~2.11), $\mathbf{D}(\bm{H}^{-1}_{\bm{\psi},M})$ is the full Hilbert space and thus $\bm{H}^{-1}_{\bm{\psi},M}$ extends as a bounded operator on the entire Hilbert space. As a result, (2.9) holds on $\mathbf{L}^{2}(\mathbb{R}^d,{\mathbf{e}}_M)$.
